checks.claim: R1 L:planar-endpoints (Lemma 8.1): covariance measures, polar/line construction, positive definiteness, Gaussian line bound S/4, Gaussian Hölder
checks.reason: SOLID. (i) Measure scaling (8.1) is equivalent to gamma(cx)=c^{-alpha}gamma(x) via Gamma(rA)=r^2∫_A gamma(ry)dy; it holds a.e. for densities. (ii) Gamma({0})=r^{2-alpha}Gamma({0}) together with local finiteness gives no atom at the origin. sigma(S^1)=(2-alpha)Gamma(B_1\{0}) is finite. S>0, since otherwise scaling would kill every ball. (iii) The annulus identity (b^{2-alpha}-a^{2-alpha})sigma(E)/(2-alpha)=∫_a^b r^{1-alpha}dr sigma(E) is correct. Uniqueness on polar rectangles gives (E:planar-polar). (iv) The endpoint polar laws dr sigma and r^{1-beta}dr sigma are correct. They are locally finite because beta<2 and tempered because of polynomial growth. Measure scaling exponents are 1 and 2-beta, by direct substitution. (v) Line mixture: evenness of sigma folds ∫_0^∞ into (1/2)∫_R. The Fourier-slice identity ∫_R psi(r omega)dr=∫_{omega^perp}|∫phi(s omega+v)ds|^2 dv >= 0 with psi=phi*phi~ is correct, and Fubini holds by Schwartz decay. (vi) Static endpoint: the subordination |x|^{-lambda}=Gamma(lambda/2)^{-1}∫s^{lambda/2-1}e^{-s|x|^2}ds is correct. Each e^{-s|x|^2}Gamma is positive definite because the Fourier transform of e^{-s|x|^2}psi is a Gaussian convolution of |phi-hat|^2 paired with the positive spectral measure. Tonelli/Fubini is justified by ∫|psi|dGamma_st<∞. (vii) Line integral of the planar wave density: ∫_{-A}^{A}ds/(2pi sqrt(A^2-s^2))=1/2 when |b|<h, and 0 otherwise. Hence (G_h*Gamma_low)(z)=(1/4)∫1{|z·omega^perp|<h}sigma(d omega)<=S/4. Evenness of G_h and p_epsilon*p_eta=p_{epsilon+eta} give (8.3) for all eta>=0 (G_{h,eta}=p_eta*G_h, G_{h,0}=G_h, canonical.tex l.1227). I independently cross-checked through the spectral side: Gamma_low has spectral unit-ball mass S/(2pi), and the inherited alpha=1 bound pi V/2 also gives S/4. (viii) theta=(beta-alpha)/(beta-1) in (0,1), and theta(alpha-1)+(1-theta)(alpha-beta)=0. Hölder with exponents 1/theta and 1/(1-theta) applies to the unnormalized finite measure p_epsilon(z-x)Gamma(dx), which has no origin atom. The physical angular mass S is used throughout; no spectral mass is substituted.

checks.claim: R2 L:planar-static-input (Lemma 8.2): generalized static source input, zero case, finite variational M, all-order coefficient rate
checks.reason: SOLID. Zero case: U_n=0 for n>=1, so B_k=0 and C_st=1 works. Fourier homogeneity: Xi(rA)=r^{2-beta}Xi(A) implies mu_Xi(rA)=r^beta mu_Xi(A), checked with test functions f(·/r). The dyadic bound ∫(1+|xi|^2)^{-1}dmu<=mu(B_1)(1+2^beta Σ2^{j(beta-2)}) is correct, so Dalang's condition (Chen-Hu (1.6), p.2146) holds. Imported premises check out against the source pages. Chen-Hu Theorem 3.8(i) (p.2165) needs only Dalang. The product/Wick formulas (2.17)/(2.19) (pp.2151-2152) give nonnegative pairing sums over all splits l1+l2=2k, including zero orders. Chen-Hu Theorem 1.2 (p.2147) requires 0<alpha<2∧d; here beta in (1,2) and d=2, with data (1,0). Chen-Hu p.2175 identifies the Chen 2023 square-root variation with 2^{alpha/(4-alpha)}M, read here with exponent beta. Chen 2023 Thm 1.1 (p.2) states finiteness under (1.3) for generalized nonnegative nonnegative-definite gamma, so M<∞ and the right side of (5.15) is finite. (5.1) with p=2 gives B_k(t)=t^{(4-beta)k}B_k(1). (5.15) with p=2 gives a finite limsup. Choosing R above the limsup and enlarging the constant to dominate the finitely many earlier k-th roots yields (E:planar-static-input) for all k>=1. No Riesz specialization is used.

checks.claim: R3 P:planar-upper (Proposition 8.3): parameters, common discrete/time/spatial Hölder, low-endpoint bound, static and target limits, exponents, full series
checks.reason: SOLID. Parameters: alpha0<theta<2-alpha<1 is nonempty, b0 is in (0,1), beta-alpha=theta(alpha-1)/(1-theta)>0, 2-beta=(2-alpha-theta)/(1-theta)>0, and (beta-alpha)/(beta-1)=theta, so Lemma 8.1 applies with weight theta. Condition (1.5) of Chen p.3 follows from spectral ball growth r^alpha and alpha<2-alpha0. Measure nu_{k,t}: its spatial mass is ∏h_l (Chen (2.4)), so it is finite. Q_delta<=T_{alpha0}=T_{b0}^theta, because gamma^0_delta (Chen (2.24)) is the truncation of the full Laplace integral equal to |u|^{-alpha0}. The edge width is 2epsilon (Chen (2.9)), and Lemma 8.1 applied edgewise gives H_Gamma<=H_low^theta H_st^{1-theta}. Hölder on nu (discrete variables included) gives (E:planar-coefficient-holder) without interpolating different temporal kernels. Low endpoint: the descending-label invariant of L:d1-spatial (Section 5, canonical l.1043-1117) is dimension-free. Each closing label gives <=S/4 by (8.3), uniformly in z; each opening label gives h_l. AM-GM with Σ opening h<=2t gives (S/2)^k t^k/k^k. The time sum is fully symmetric, each pairing integrates to (Z_{b0}t^{2-b0})^k with Z_b=2/((1-b)(2-b)), and Σ_m 1/(m!(2k-m)!)=4^k/(2k)!, giving 2^k Z^k t^{(2-b0)k}/k!. The product is (Z_{b0}S)^k t^{(3-b0)k}/(k!k^k)<=C_low^k t^{(3-b0)k}/(k!)^2. B_k^epsilon is exactly the Chen-Hu regularized static coefficient at width 2epsilon (p.2152) after the chain form of (2.12). Limits: the bound on L is uniform and deterministic, the target orders converge by Chen Thm 4.1 (p.22; common widths are a special case), and the static orders converge by Chen-Hu Thm 3.8(i). Products converge in L^1 and only 2k+1 splits occur. Lemma 8.2 is applied only after the limit. Exponents: 2theta+(1-theta)(3-beta)=3-alpha and theta(3-b0)+(1-theta)(4-beta)=4-alpha-alpha0 both verified. Series: Σa_k^q<=(Σa_k)^q for q>=1 gives exp(qC^{1/q}t^kappa), with A_0=1 and the full nonnegative series from P:mixed. A_k matches its inherited definition (canonical l.1123).

checks.claim: R4 C:planar-range (Corollary 8.4) and R:planar-scope (Remark 8.5): boundary cases and residual open items
checks.reason: SOLID. Case 0<alpha<=1 (including alpha=1, allowed in d=2) uses P:low-alpha-upper. Its V=mu(B_1) is a spectral ball mass (canonical l.1225), and V>0 whenever the covariance is nonzero by spectral homogeneity. Case 1<alpha<2-alpha0 uses P:planar-upper, with theta fixed canonically. Gamma=0 gives u=1 and C_2=0. Hypothesis H:homog with d=2 forces alpha<2, so the corollary covers all of 0<alpha<2-alpha0. Remark: kappa tends to (4-alpha)/(3-alpha) as alpha0 decreases to 0, matching Chen-Hu (1.9), with no interchange of limits claimed. Cauchy-Schwarz gives E u<=exp(qC^{1/q}t^kappa/2). P:Jensen gives 2L_*<=qC^{1/q}; this is a consistency inequality, not a sharp constant. Balan-Conus (pp.1489-1494) concerns Skorohod/Malliavin solutions with fBm time and Riesz-type cases (i)-(iv); it is correctly treated as comparison only. The remark correctly leaves open: d=3 for alpha>1, the sharp constant, novelty, and formal verification.

checks.claim: R5a weighted-tool.md: standalone (WC) sufficiency estimate, ordinary-G corollary, smoothing scope (independent of Section 8)
checks.reason: SOLID. Scaling to h=1: both sides have degree 1-alpha. Time density: the support is a<u<1-b. With u=a+L sin^2 theta the integrand becomes 2dtheta/sqrt((2a+L sin^2)(2b+L cos^2)), and the constant is 1/(2pi^2). The two tangent substitutions give E(k)/sqrt(D) with D=1-(a-b)^2, k=4ab/D, and D-4ab=1-(a+b)^2>0. (EL): the split at pi/4, sin v>=2v/pi, and ∫_0^{pi/4}dv/sqrt(4v^2/pi^2+k/2)=(pi/2)asinh(1/sqrt(2k)) are correct, and asinh x<=log(1+2x) holds. Section 4 (1/2<=z<1) on a<=b: a<=1/2, b>=1/4, D>=max(delta,4a(1-a))>=(delta+a)/2. Both sign cases of z-2a give D<=delta+4a. Hence k>=a/(4(delta+a)) and C_N=sqrt2 C_E(1+log4)/(2pi^2). (RR) layer-cake disk comparison is correct, so I<=4pi C_N J. The J evaluation via r=delta s gives B_alpha, and delta^{3/2-alpha}<=delta^{1/2-q} exactly when q>=alpha-1. At alpha=3/2 the log loss is absorbed with delta^eta log(1/delta)<=1/(e eta). Section 7 (z<1/2): D>3/4, C_F=C_E/(pi^2 sqrt3), B_F=1/(2-alpha)+1/(2-alpha)^2. Assembly with G_1(Z)^{2q-1}=(2pi)^{1-2q}delta^{1/2-q} gives C_{alpha,q}. Corollary 8a: G_h>=1/(2pi h) on support, so G^p<=(2pi h)^{1-p}G with total power 2-alpha; q=alpha/2 is admissible. The smoothing scope is stated correctly: covariance-only smoothing works by averaging over W, while Green-smoothed kernels with the same compactly supported right side fail. The note's scope disclaimers (no all-order iteration, no d3, no anisotropic case, no moment theorem) are accurate. Nothing in Section 8 depends on this note.

checks.claim: R5b boundary-probe.md: necessity q>=alpha-1 and coincident-point finiteness
checks.reason: SOLID. On the cell eps/4<u<eps/2, |y|<eps/16, |Z-(1-eps)e1|<eps/16, |W|<eps/16: G_u>=1/(pi eps); |Z-y| lies in (1-9eps/8,1-7eps/8) and (1-u)^2-|Z-y|^2<=9eps/4, so G_{1-u}>=1/(3pi sqrt eps); and |W-y|^{-alpha}>=8^alpha eps^{-alpha}. With cell volume (eps/4)pi(eps/16)^2 this gives (LB) 8^alpha eps^{3/2-alpha}/(3072pi), arithmetic verified. Also |Z|<=1-15eps/16 gives G_1(Z)^{2q-1}<=A_q eps^{1/2-q}. So (WC) would force eps^{1+q-alpha}<=const, which fails on open sets when q<alpha-1. Time/space reversal gives I(1;Z,W)=I(1;Z,Z-W). The coincident case: the K(r) bounds 4sqrt2 arcosh(1/(2r))<=4sqrt2 log(1/r) and 2pi (beta integral) are correct, so I(1;0,0)<∞ for alpha<2. The necessity is consistent with the weighted-tool sufficiency, so the threshold q=alpha-1 (alpha>3/2) is internally consistent across the two documents.

checks.claim: R6 Combined application and scope audit: no missing new dependency, imported premises verified, constant scope, anisotropic/d3/sharp/novelty/Lean boundaries
checks.reason: SOLID. Section 8 cites only H:homog, P:mixed, T:first, P:Jensen, P:low-alpha-upper, L:d1-spatial (all in Sections 2-5; L:d1-spatial only for the descending-label procedure, which Section 8 restates) and its own lemmas. No Section 6/7 statement, and nothing from weighted-tool.md or boundary-probe.md, is a premise. Every imported hypothesis was checked against the source images: Chen (1.5) p.3 and Thm 4.1 p.22; Chen (2.9)/(2.24) pp.8,13; Chen-Hu (1.6), Thm 1.2, (2.17)/(2.19), Thm 3.8(i), (5.1), (5.15), p.2175; Chen 2023 Thm 1.1. No retroactive constant change occurs. C depends on Gamma, alpha0 and the fixed theta, as stated, and the per-k bounds are uniform in k, t, x. Physical S (Lemma 8.1) and spectral V (P:low-alpha-upper) are kept separate. Anisotropic planar covariances, including singular line-supported measures, are covered because no angular density is used. d=3 with alpha>1, the sharp constant, novelty and Lean are explicitly left open. No full-goal clearance is claimed.

minor: SYMBOL-COLLISION (L:planar-endpoints, Lemma 8.1, proof): Gamma denotes the covariance measure, but Gamma(lambda/2) in the subordination formula is the Euler Gamma function. Meaning is recoverable from context, but a distinct symbol would help.

SYMBOL-COLLISION (Section 8 vs inherited context): beta is a free parameter in Lemma 8.1, an exponent in Lemma 8.2 and a theta-derived quantity in Proposition 8.3. The inherited Section G0 and P:low-alpha-upper (invoked in Corollary 8.4) use beta=4-alpha-alpha0. Each use is locally defined, but a reader of C:planar-range sees both meanings.
SYMBOL-COLLISION (L:planar-static-input, Lemma 8.2, proof): mu_Xi(B_1) uses B_1 for the unit ball while B_k(t) is the static coefficient, so B_1 is ambiguous at k=1.

Packet context gap (not a mathematical gap): G_{h,eta}=p_eta*G_h with G_{h,0}=G_h, the definition A_k(t)=Σ_m E[X_mX_{2k-m}], V=mu(B_1), and L:d1-spatial are used by Section 8 and P:low-alpha-upper but are absent from context.txt. They were confirmed in canonical.tex lines 1043-1123 and 1223-1227.

The opening equivalence claim (measure scaling (8.1) equivalent to Hypothesis H:homog) holds for densities only up to a.e. representatives. For generalized covariances it is the distributional homogeneity also used in Section 5 (canonical l.1221-1222). A one-phrase qualification would make this explicit.

Proposition 8.3 remarks that the low endpoint's spectral exponent is one with b0<1, as if existence results were needed for it. L_k^epsilon is purely deterministic and needs no stochastic import; the sentence is harmless but redundant.

C:planar-range (Corollary 8.4) says C_2 depends on alpha0 and the covariance. For 1<alpha<2-alpha0 it also depends on the chosen theta, unless theta is fixed canonically (e.g., the midpoint of (alpha0,2-alpha)). Stating that choice would remove the ambiguity.

limitations: This is an AI fresh-replay review, not human verification and not a novelty audit. The adversarial skeptic and final whole-paper cold read were out of scope.

Imported theorems were checked only as stated on the supplied rendered pages: Chen-Hu Thm 3.8(i), (2.17)/(2.19), Thm 1.2 with (5.1)/(5.15) and the p.2175 identification; Chen 2023 Thm 1.1; Chen author-manuscript Thm 4.1, (1.5), (2.9), (2.24). Their internal proofs (e.g., (5.11)/(5.13) constants, Appendix A.2) were not re-derived.

The application of Chen-Hu Section 5 to Xi=Gamma_st assumes the source's generalized-covariance framework covers every nonnegative positive-definite homogeneous measure, including singular (e.g., line-supported) anisotropic ones. The source explicitly includes generalized gamma (the delta_0 example, p.2146-2147, p.2152) and Chen 2023 allows generalized gamma, so I accept this as imported scope. A source author's confirmation would remove residual uncertainty.

P:mixed, P:low-alpha-upper, P:Jensen and T:first were treated as inherited inputs, not re-reviewed. L:d1-spatial and P:low-alpha-upper were read in canonical.tex only to confirm definitions and the descending-label invariant.

canonical.pdf and the full paper PDFs were not opened. No compilation, hash, or line-identity check of section8.txt against canonical.tex lines 2232-2691 was run; reading-map.json's binding was accepted as stated.

Self-check: correctness replay of Section 8, weighted-tool.md and boundary-probe.md found no fatal/major defect. This is not gold-standard certification of the paper: d=3 with alpha>1, sharp constants, novelty and Lean verification remain open, and the weighted-tool/boundary-probe notes remain unadopted standalone candidates.
